From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@fintechco.com>, Sam Patel <sam.p@paymentlabs.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated - latency/throughput follow-up

Hi Alex / Sam,

Thanks again for taking time this morning — great conversation and super helpful context on your production load. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can get you the right recommendation between Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity: 

- Production profile you shared: ~4000 RPS sustained for settlement pipeline, spiky bursts to ~8k RPS during peak windows; tight p95 latency targets of ~50ms for in-path scoring requests.
- Data/tenant needs: single-tenant isolation preferred for sensitive PII-processing flows; other non-PII workloads could run on shared Hosted.

Questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Are the 50ms p95 and 4k sustained numbers for a single model/route, or distributed across multiple routes? (This affects batching strategy.)
2) Do you expect traffic to be uniform across hours or heavily time-of-day gated (we saw traffic spikes in your example at 02:00 UTC)?

Preliminary guidance:
- Hosted API: Fastest path to get started. Good for lower sustained volumes and if you can tolerate some multi-tenant variability. We can support bursty traffic via autoscaling but sustained 4k RPS with strict 50ms p95 is likely to see higher cost or inconsistent latency on Hosted.
- Dedicated: Recommended for sustained high throughput + tight latency SLOs. Dedicated capacity gives predictable GPU pools, reserved throughput, and control over autoscaling policies. For FinTechCo's numbers, Dedicated will likely be the right baseline for the scoring pipeline.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Consider if you require private networking and customer-managed infra; adds ops overhead but provides max isolation.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm answers to Q1/Q2 above?
- If you're comfortable, we can run a short performance trial on Dedicated (2-4 weeks) for the scoring route to validate latency at target throughput. We'll provide a datadog/tracing dashboard and tokenized test harness.

Attaching a quick TCO worksheet so you can plug in numbers (redwood_tco_calc.xlsx).

If helpful I can loop in Rishi (capacity planning) and one of our infra engineers for a technical deep dive. What does your availability look like this week or early next?

Thanks,

Alex — thanks, that helps a lot. Short answers up front: Dedicated is the recommended path for predictable p95 <= 50ms at sustained 4k RPS with spikes to 8k RPS.

Why Dedicated for your profile:
- Predictable GPU pools: Dedicated gives reserved instance capacity so you don't compete with other tenants for scheduling, which is the main source of p95 variance on Hosted.
- Autoscale predictability: With Dedicated we can set throughput-guaranteed pools and pre-warm KV caches for the scoring route to avoid cold-cache tails.
- Cost: Hosted can be competitive for smaller/ephemeral workloads, but sustained RPS at your scale tends to be cheaper on Dedicated once you account for cache misses and higher autoscale headroom. I attached our Dedicated options doc with recommended pool sizes for your input (dedicated-options.pdf).

Warmup / KV Cache notes:
- We'll instrument a priming job during rollouts to populate KV caches and maintain a small steady-state traffic to keep caches warm. That reduces tail latency on scale-ups.
- During the trial we will run synthetic priming and measure p50/p95/p99 across multiple sequences to validate.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep dive Thurs 19 Mar, 2:30pm PST — we'll include Rishi (capacity) and one infra engineer to go through pooling and priming plan.
2) 2-week Dedicated trial scoped to the scoring model (we'll provide a test harness and metrics dashboard).
3) After trial, we'll review TCO and finalize a Dedicated sizing + SLA.

Can you confirm Thurs 2:30pm PST works and if we should add any of your platform/ops folks to the call?
